title: Sanshin (Okinawan three-string lute)
summary: The sanshin is the three-string lute of Okinawa. Its oval body is covered with python skin, and its long neck has no frets. Players pick the strings with a small plectrum worn on the finger, and the island scale of five notes gives its songs a sunny, open sound.
howToPlay: Three strings run down the neck, the thickest on the left. The neck has no frets: each lane marks the finger place of a note.
A bead slides down the string to its place. Pick the lane as the bead lands.
Open lanes at the top sound the string without pressing.
Try the island walk first, then the swaying line, then the quick dance.
rules: The notes come from the island scale: C, E, F, G and B, in two octaves.
Every phrase is played through twice.
A pick on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra picks cost points.
The quick dance has two beats to the bar; the others have four.
heritageNote: The sanshin has been played in Okinawa for about six hundred years. Folk songs, dances and village gatherings are all led by it, and makers still cover the oval body with carefully chosen skin.
